item.title: Pi-Ener-lite – A compact 18650 UPS board for Raspberry Pi Zero with RTC and fuel gauge
item.description: Designed by ACE Design Studio in China, the Pi-Ener-lite is a dedicated UPS board made specifically for the Raspberry Pi Zero series. It features a standard flat-top 18650 lithium-ion battery holder and switches to battery power when external power is lost, while supporting simultaneous charging and discharging. The Pi-Ener-lite connects to the bottom of the Raspberry Pi Zero via seven spring-loaded pogo pins that handle both power delivery and I2C data communication, leaving the top GPIO header free for other HATs or expansions. Pi-Ener-lite specifications: Compatibility – Raspberry Pi Zero series SBCs USB – 1x USB Type-C port for charging Misc Power switch DS1307 real-time clock (RTC) chip with a CR1220 coin cell battery holder 7x spring pogo pins for power delivery and I2C data Power Management Battery Support – Standard flat-top 18650 lithium-ion cell; supports simultaneous charging and discharging Charging current – 1A @ 5V Output current – 2.5A [...] The post Pi-Ener-lite – A compact 18650 UPS board for Raspberry Pi Zero with RTC and fuel gauge appeared first on CNX Software - Embedded Systems News.

item.title: Luckfox Lyra PLC – A Linux-based Rockchip RK3506B industrial controller with RS232, RS422, RS485, CAN bus, and relays
item.description: Luckfox Lyra PLC is a Linux-based programmable logic controller powered by a Rockchip RK3506B tri-core Arm Cortex-A7 SoC, equipped with dual Ethernet, WiFi 6 and Bluetooth 5.2 wireless connectivity, a 1.9-inch touchscreen LCD, and a range of I/Os. The I/Os are mostly exposed through two 11-pole terminal blocks with one RS232, one shared RS422/RS485, one CAN Bus, and two relays, as well as smaller connectors for I2C, GPIO, and debugging. The system can be powered via USB-C (5V only), terminal block pins supporting 7V-24V DC input, or an optional PoE module. item.title: Google Chrome is now available for Arm Linux. We tested it on a Raspberry Pi 5
item.description: Google Chrome web browser is now available for 64-bit Arm Linux, and we quickly tested it with Raspberry Pi OS on a Raspberry Pi 5 2GB SBC. The open-source Google Chromium web browser has been available for Arm Linux for years, but it lacks some features such as account sync, out-of-the-box DRM support, and automatic updates. Google wrote about working on a port last March, but hasn’t officially released it. However, users on Interfacing Linux have noticed that it can easily be installed by changing amd64 to arm64 in the download link. So we did that on a Raspberry Pi 5: [crayon-6a830f3fae1e5761796087/] Google Chrome now appears alongside Chromium and Firefox in the list of Internet applications. The screenshot below shows that some GPU features like WebGL and video acceleration are enabled. The latter is not especially useful on a Raspberry Pi 5 since the Broadcom BCM2712 only supports H.265 hardware [...] The post Google Chrome is now available for Arm Linux. item.title: EITWatch open-source ESP32-S3 smartwatch implements planar EIT hand gesture recognition
item.description: Researchers from Northwestern University have introduced EITWatch, an open-source ESP32-S3-based EIT (Electrical Impedance Tomography) gesture-sensing system that fits within a standard smartwatch footprint. It relies on a Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 board and eight electrodes arranged on the back of the case to detect hand gestures via impedance changes caused by muscle and tendon movement beneath the skin. Unlike other wrist-EIT systems that use circumferential electrode bands, EITWatch places all eight electrodes on the back of the smartwatch case. The sensing area consists of a 31 mm electrode ring that fits within a standard 40 mm watch case, while a 20 mm PCB extension carries the discrete analog front end (AFE). EITWatch hardware specifications: Wireless board – XIAO ESP32-S3 SoC – Espressif ESP32-S3R8 CPU – Dual-core Tensilica LX7 microcontroller up to 240 MHz with vector instructions for AI acceleration Memory – 512KB SRAM, 8MB PSRAM Wireless – Wi-Fi 4 and [...] The post EITWatch open-source ESP32-S3 smartwatch implements planar EIT hand gesture recognition appeared first on CNX Software - Embedded Systems News.

item.description: Gemma Translator is an open-source project for the Raspberry Pi 5 that acts as a multilingual interpreter running locally without access to the cloud using Google Gemma 4 and LiteRT runtime. It’s a project built by three Google engineers with the help of Google Antigravity. It includes code to run an on-device, fully offline voice translator/interpreter using Gemma 4 E2B (2.3B effective / ~5.1B total parameters with per-layer embeddings) and the LiteRT runtime. item.title: PewCB One Desktop PCB fabrication system enables rapid prototyping at home
item.description: PewCB One is a desktop PCB prototyping system designed to accelerate hardware development by manufacturing PCBs at home or in the office in a few hours or less, instead of waiting days for a PCB to come back from the factory. Unlike desktop fabrication methods that rely on chemical processing, the PewCB One is more akin to a fully enclosed laser engraver housed with an integrated air filtration system. Users can perform the full process from double-sided PCB blanks to a complete PCBA at home. item.title: Comu is a $6 tiny CH32V203 RISC-V development board that fits inside a USB port
item.description: Over the years, we have seen several tiny “omu” USB boards that share this “fits-in-a-USB-port” form factor. It started with the Tomu, based on a Silicon Labs EFM32 Cortex-M0+, followed by the Fomu with a Lattice iCE40 FPGA, Qomu with an EOS S3 Cortex-M4F MCU and FPGA, and the Somu, a tiny FIDO2 security key. Icy Electronics has now introduced Comu, another tiny development board based on the 144 MHz WCH CH32V203 RISC-V MCU. While measuring just 13 x 9.4 mm (slightly smaller than a microSD card), the board still packs two white LEDs, four capacitive touch buttons, and six GPIOs exposed through test pads. It is designed for bare-metal programming, custom USB HID projects, and USB packet experimentation. Comu specifications: MCU – WCH CH32V203V203F8 CPU – Single-core 32-bit RISC-V clocked at 144MHz Memory – 20KB SRAM Storage – 224KB Flash (64KB of 0-wait Flash and 160KB of normal Flash) [...] The post Comu is a $6 tiny CH32V203 RISC-V development board that fits inside a USB port appeared first on CNX Software - Embedded Systems News.

item.title: MaTouch ESP32-S3 MaUWB board integrates 3.95-inch touchscreen and UWB module for indoor positioning and ranging
item.description: Makerfabs MaTouch ESP32-S3 MaUWB is a development board that combines an ESP32-S3 wireless MCU, a 3.95-inch touchscreen display, and a UWB module for indoor positioning and ranging applications. The board can be used as a portable positioning terminal. It uses a trilateration algorithm with up to three fixed UWB anchors to calculate the tag’s coordinates in real time. The MaUWB chipset operates on UWB Channel 5 (6489.6 MHz) and supports up to 8 anchors and 64 tags. For portable use, the board includes a LiPo battery connector, charging circuit, and battery level monitoring. item.title: Proxmox VE now officially supports 64-bit Arm (Aarch64) targets
item.description: Proxmox has recently announced the first official release of Proxmox Virtual Environment (VE) with support for 64-bit Arm (arm64/aarch64). Until now, the popular virtualization solution was only available for x86-64 (amd64). Proxmox VE 9.2 for arm64 is built on Debian 13.5 “Trixie” with Linux 7.0, and is otherwise based on the same code as the x86-64 version, and relies on the same configuration, tooling, and documentation, except for a few architecture-specific differences. The developers note that Proxmox VE for Arm fully supports NVIDIA Grace Hopper and NVIDIA Vera platforms, and “best-effort” support is available on other UEFI-based Armv8-A/Armv9-A hardware. However, device-tree-only single-board computers, such as the Raspberry Pi, are not supported, since the host must boot through UEFI and describe its hardware through ACPI. Having said that, we previously noted work on an UEFI+ACPI port for the Raspberry Pi 4, and users have already managed to have the release work [...] The post Proxmox VE now officially supports 64-bit Arm (Aarch64) targets appeared first on CNX Software - Embedded Systems News.
